slides.title: IBM Bob 2.0
slides.subtitle: What's new
slides.notes: Title slide. One sentence on what changed and why it matters to the audience.

slides.title: 2.0 changes the feel of the work
slides.takeaway: The biggest speed gain comes from parallel, native tool calling, not from the larger context window.
slides.notes: Lead with the felt difference, then the numbers.

slides.title: Three modes replace five
cards: Takes action and completes the task.
Investigates, resolves requirements, and produces an actionable handoff.
Explains architecture and behaviour without changing the codebase.
slides.takeaway: Code becomes Agent. Advanced and Orchestrator fold into the three. You can switch modes without starting over.
slides.notes: Tall cards overlap the band on purpose - the ACE-deck pattern.

slides.title: Bob can do more without interrupting you
cards: Approved by default, so Bob can gather context without stopping.
Run in separate threads without taking over your screen.
Work in separate contexts and return focused summaries.
slides.takeaway: State-changing actions follow your approval settings.
slides.notes: Three light cards; the default content slide.

slides.title: Other changes in 2.0
cards: Workflows can now call other workflows.
Workflows for Java modernisation, IBM i, and IBM Z.
Update the Bob extension. Settings, rules, and MCP servers carry over.
Restore file state per task, conversation turn, or tool call.
slides.note: Keep the list short; the details live in the release notes.
slides.notes: Left panel slide for a grab-bag of four.

slides.title: Skills
slides.subtitle: Turn "do this" into "always do this the same way"

slides.title: A skill is reusable guidance Bob can follow
cards: Instructions for one specific kind of work.
Activate it yourself, or let Bob match it from the description.
No duplicate instructions in the same conversation.
Can include checklists, templates, examples, and references.
slides.takeaway: A prompt asks for an outcome. A skill captures how your team produces it.
slides.notes: Four cards get the taller heading box automatically.

slides.title: Small file, explicit contract
bullets: Project skills live in `.bob/skills/`; global skills in `~/.bob/skills/`
Bob uses the description to decide when the skill applies
Skill activation asks for approval by default; that can be auto-approved in settings
slides.notes: Code panel left, three bullets right. Comments render teal.

slides.title: The three built-in modes
items: "How does authentication flow through this repository?"
"Design the Java 17 migration and identify the risky assumptions."
"Implement the approved migration plan and verify it."
slides.footer: Match the mode to the uncertainty.
slides.notes: Purple full-bleed with flat teal glyphs.

slides.title: The 5 available hooks
slides.lead: Bob reaches a known point in its lifecycle and runs a configured shell command.
items: Inject context once, before the first turn.
Add context, or reject the prompt with exit code 2.
Validate or block a matched tool before it runs.
Log or verify after a matched tool completes.
Run cleanup or write a report when Bob finishes.
statement: only UserPromptSubmit and PreToolUse can block.
slides.notes: Quote layout reused as a list-plus-statement slide.

slides.title: Bob 2.0 in one sentence
slides.subtitle: Faster execution, simpler modes, and team knowledge you can reuse without giving up explicit control.
slides.notes: Closing sentence before the template closer.
